entities.summary:
Polemon II of Pontus, also known as Marcus Antonius Polemon Pythodoros, was a prince of the Bosporan, Pontus, Cilicia, and Cappadocia, serving as a Roman client king of Pontus, Colchis, and Cilicia. 

Born into a prominent family, Polemon II's early life and ascension to power are shrouded in mystery. He succeeded his father, Polemon I, as king of Pontus in 56 CE. 

Polemon II's reign was marked by diplomatic efforts to maintain the region's autonomy in the face of Roman expansion. He engaged in a series of negotiations with Roman emperors, including Nero and Trajan, to secure the region's status as a Roman client state. 

Despite these efforts, Polemon II's reign was cut short when he died in 74 CE, reportedly due to illness. His death led to a succession crisis, with his cousin, Polemon III, eventually seizing the throne. 

Polemon II's legacy extends beyond his own reign, as he played a key role in shaping the region's politics and culture. His diplomatic efforts and strategic alliances helped maintain the region's independence for several decades. 

In the centuries following his death, Polemon II's reputation as a shrewd politician and strategist has endured. He remains a fascinating figure in the history of the ancient world, offering valuable insights into the complexities of regional politics and diplomacy.
